author: DTrim99
body:
Confirmed — you're exactly right. PolicyEngine computes the inflationary relief credit with the joint-return table even though this couple is filing combined (status 4), and that's too generous.

For a combined return the credit is looked up **per spouse in the single-filer table** (max $150, reduced $10 per $1,000 above $87,000, gone at $101,000):
- Primary net income $90,877 → **$110**
- Spouse net income $165,258 → **$0** (over $101,000)
- Total = **$110** — AR1000TC line 7, matching TaxAct (AR1000F line 36 = 110, net tax line 38 = 11,925).

PolicyEngine instead uses the **joint** table (max $300, phase-out from $174,000) and splits it 50/50, so each spouse gets $150 → **$300** total. That drops PE's Arkansas net tax to $11,739 vs TaxAct's $11,925 — the ~$186 gap is the $190 over-credit, net of a ~$4 rounding difference in tax before credits. PE's per-spouse net incomes ($90,877 / $165,258) match your worksheet exactly, so the table selection is the only difference.

Root cause: the credit keys its table off filing status, which is "joint" for any married couple, so combined filers wrongly get the $300/$174,000 schedule instead of the per-spouse $150/$87,000 one. Fix is to use the single-filer table per spouse whenever the couple files combined.

And you're right that this feeds back into the combined-vs-joint choice — the credit is now $110 combined vs $0 joint, so the selection should weigh it (PE already does this for the additional tax credit for qualified individuals, but not yet for this one; noted as follow-up). Filed as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9320, fix on the way.
